# Adhd

This folder catalogs the specific pharmacological treatments for ADHD tracked within the Danish national ADHD database quality monitoring system. It covers both stimulant and non-stimulant medications, detailing their inclusion in key clinical quality indicators like Indikator 6 for children and adolescents, and the newly introduced Indikator 11 for adults. Each page outlines the medication's ATC code, its role in measuring treatment coverage across Danish regions, and its exact mentions and relationships within the national registry reports.

## Pages

- [[atomoxetin-n06ba09|Atomoxetin (N06BA09)]] — A non-stimulant norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor tracked in both youth and adult quality indicators to measure pharmacological treatment coverage.
- [[dexamfetamin-n06ba02|Dexamfetamin (N06BA02)]] — A stimulant medication evaluated to assess the systemic balance of pharmacological treatments across different Danish regions and departments.
- [[guanfacin-c02ac02|Guanfacin (C02AC02)]] — A secondary treatment option often used for patients with comorbidities, integrated into national metrics to capture the full spectrum of medical interventions.
- [[lisdexamfetamin-n06ba12|Lisdexamfetamin (N06BA12)]] — An extended-duration prodrug of dexamfetamine that serves as a key metric for clinical quality development and political steering of ADHD care.
- [[methylphenidat-n06ba04|Methylphenidat (N06BA04)]] — The most common ADHD medication in Denmark, heavily monitored to highlight regional variations and implementation strengths such as those in North Jutland.
- [[modafinil-n06ba07|Modafinil (N06BA07)]] — An alternative treatment used under specific clinical conditions, tracked to ensure comprehensive monitoring of medication practices across all demographics.
